all.title: File:Köenig Air Rider Wildcat (52691296876).jpg
all.artist: Alan Wilson from Peterborough, Cambs, UK
all.description:
Produced in the early 1990’s, this 4-seat hovercraft was powered by a 150hp 4-stroke turbo-diesel engine. It was expected to have a range of 150miles and to sell for around $200,000. The company also marketed the single-seat Booster and two-seat Hunter as alternative models.

all.title: File:Hover Air Hoverhawk HA5 ‘No003’ (52691714670).jpg
all.artist: Alan Wilson from Peterborough, Cambs, UK
all.description:
c/n HA5-003
Built in 1968, this appears to be a pre-production example of this popular British hovercraft design. Peterborough based Hover Air built a total of 121 HA5s between 1967 and 1971, making it the first mass-produced two-seat hovercraft.
Château de Savigny-lès-Beaune, France

12th May 2022

all.artist: Alan Wilson from Peterborough, Cambs, UK
all.description:
Wearing French military roundels, this appears to be a turbine powered hovercraft. It is also marked as having an ejector seat, which I rather doubt, so may just be a mock-up.
Any info on this machine would be very welcome.
Château de Savigny-lès-Beaune, France

Previously on display with the Blois Aero Club, she became part of the collection here during July 1987.
Château de Savigny-lès-Beaune, France

all.title: File:Köenig Air Rider Wildcat (52691296876).jpg
all.artist: Alan Wilson from Peterborough, Cambs, UK
all.description:
Produced in the early 1990’s, this 4-seat hovercraft was powered by a 150hp 4-stroke turbo-diesel engine. It was expected to have a range of 150miles and to sell for around $200,000. The company also marketed the single-seat Booster and two-seat Hunter as alternative models.
Château de Savigny-lès-B

all.title: File:Hover Air Hoverhawk HA5 ‘No003’ (52691714670).jpg
all.artist: Alan Wilson from Peterborough, Cambs, UK
all.description:
c/n HA5-003
Built in 1968, this appears to be a pre-production example of this popular British hovercraft design. Peterborough based Hover Air built a total of 121 HA5s between 1967 and 1971, making it the first mass-produced two-seat hovercraft.
Château de Savigny-lès-Beaune, France

12th May 2022

all.title: File:Unknown turbine-powered hovercraft (52691767305).jpg
all.artist: Alan Wilson from Peterborough, Cambs, UK
all.description:
Wearing French military roundels, this appears to be a turbine powered hovercraft. It is also marked as having an ejector seat, which I rather doubt, so may just be a mock-up.
Any info on this machine would be very welcome.
Château de Savigny-lès-Beaune, France
